[Music] My name is Sudheer Kumar, I am from Thiruvananthapuram. Today,
coming to this altar, to share the testimony I received, to give witness to the Gospel—this opportunity given to me by the infinitely good Mother,
no matter how much thanks I offer, it will never be enough, because
I am going to share a very great testimony. It is about my eldest son—his name is Dinadev.
I am a person who is 100% blind. My son also is a person who is 100% blind. I have another son too, his name is Vasudev.
That child also is 100% blind. He is studying in 9th standard. This elder son has finished Plus
Two. So, what I am going to share here is about the blessing that Mother has given us.
As I said,
when this son had completed his 9th standard, during the vacation time, I asked him: “Son,
after one more year when you complete 10th, the studies that follow are of a different kind.
That means, right now you are studying all the subjects—Social Science, Geography, all such subjects. But in Plus One,
studies go in a different way. You mainly choose one particular subject,
and the other two or three will be related to it.”
When the subjects come, then after that it continues step by step, gradually increasing in difficulty. At that point,
I asked my son which field he wished to work in, and what he wanted to study.
When I asked if he had any idea in his mind, my son Dinadev clearly said without any doubt
that he wanted to study computer science, and then reach the position of a computer engineer. He said he wants
to live his entire life in the world of computers. I said, “Alright, son.”
I didn’t know how this would be possible, but I just prayed, “God, please help him.”
I told him, “Son, let’s work hard together.” That was all I said. In 2023, after passing 10th grade,
he scored A+ in all subjects. After that, following his wish, he started studying computer science
as the main subject for Plus One and Plus Two. Then the Plus Two results came, and he again scored A+
in all subjects. After that, he needed to appear for the engineering entrance exam.
So, in order to appear for the entrance exam,
we submitted the application. On the third day, a message came to his phone saying that your
application has been rejected. He was sitting there crying because of it. That evening, when I returned home from work,
my son told me something while crying: “Father, the application I submitted has been rejected. The entrance commissioner said the reason is…”
“…because I am blind.” I calmed him down and told him not to worry.
I said, “Son, it's only the entrance commissioner rejecting it. Anyway, with the intercession of the Holy Mother,
whatever we ask from the Lord will not be rejected. I have faith in that.” I reassured him,
saying, “Don’t worry, Mother will make a way for everything we need.”
But because of his age and immaturity, he couldn’t feel completely at peace.
That evening, while I was praying, Mother gave me a message. She told me to ask those authorities on what basis
they were rejecting the application. If it was because he is blind, then I needed to request them to show me
any rule or regulation that says that blind people cannot study engineering.
I was instructed to demand that they provide it if such a rule existed. The next day, I went to the commissioner’s office,
submitted a written request, and after two days, another message came saying that the application
has been accepted. Then the date for the entrance exam was scheduled.
Now, my son could not write the exam by himself; he needed a scribe. So, I applied for a scribe order.
When we submitted the application, they said that only students who have completed Plus One can write with a scribe.
That means a junior student can do it. So, we submitted the marks list of a student who had passed Plus One, and everything…
They said that the application must be accompanied by this, and returned it. Okay, I found a student studying in 11th grade,
spoke to the child’s guardians, and obtained their consent. Then, submitting the application along with all their details,
they said we would need the Plus One marks list. It would take about a month and a half for the results to come,
and only after the results come can the marks list be provided. When I asked about this, they said
it was a rule from the authorities. One thing to do: Check that the student has studied in 10th grade,
go to that school, meet the headmaster, and confirm that the student studied there,
and that the student passed with these marks. Get it written and stamped on official letterhead. I agreed,
and together with my son and that student and the student’s guardians, I went to the school. At that time, the headmaster was there.
When I explained the matter in full, they were completely uncooperative. They refused to help. That is, the student is currently in 11th grade,
but they were refusing to certify that a 10th-grade student studied in their school. The reason they gave for insisting to do it that day was very low-minded.
They repeated it multiple times. But in no way did the headmaster cooperate. In this troubling situation,
I took the covenant medal I usually carry in my pocket, held it tightly, and while reciting a prayer of faith,
I said to Mother very humbly, “Mother, I cannot ignore this opposition. Please help me.” I spoke sincerely,
saying, “Even though I am blind, Mother, I need your help.” I am blind due to glaucoma,
and tears came to my eyes despite never having cried much before. I was very distressed.
At that moment, the door opened, and a lady entered the room. She was wearing an anklet that made a sound as she walked.
You could hear the sound clearly, and it smelled faintly of jasmine flowers. There may have been a flower in her hair.
She came near us, stood in front of us, and said: pointing to the student who was going to be the scribe,
“This student passed 10th grade a year ago in this school, right? This is the student who will be the scribe for Dinadev.”
“Now we are going to certify that this student studied in this school, and passed 10th grade with these marks,” she said.
“This does not cause any loss to the school. It is not wrong to support something honest. This is in God’s interest.”
She handed the stamped letter to my son. The headmaster said nothing further. My son took it,
filled in all the required details, and I told him, “May God bless this with love.”
That lady had been sitting with me until then. I stood up and said,
“If you approach God with love, He will never abandon you. This you must understand first: God is always with us.”
She blessed us and left. At that time, my son Dinadev, the student who came to be the scribe,
and the student’s guardians all thanked the headmaster and left. As we walked out,
I told them, “We must find out who that lady in the school was and thank her, because it is due to her that we achieved this.”
We looked around everywhere—teachers’ room, office room, asked the security. “Was there a lady here who helped us?”
But no one saw her or could identify her. I still firmly believe that Mother appeared before us,
because until that lady came, the headmaster had refused to cooperate. After she arrived, the certification was given.
Then I took the paper and submitted it to the entrance commission’s office to get a scribe for my son.
The scribe order was received, the exam was written, and he came out with a rank of 5945, exactly according to the merit list.
He got admission in engineering exactly as per the merit list. My son wanted the AML Computer Science branch,
and he got the opportunity to study it. But what happened next is where Mother again helped me, and I can say this clearly.
Even after getting admission according to the rank list, the authorities said it was not possible to give him admission. When I asked why,
they argued with me every day. They said, “He is blind. A blind student cannot study. There is no order allowing it.
Only students with up to 40% disability are permitted for technical education by the government.” They kept giving such obstacles every day.
Every evening, when I prayed, Mother comforted me. I remember all those words. Even now,
whenever I pray, it feels like a message in my heart: “Do not fear, do
not fear. God is with you.” That was always the message, and I still remember it.
Then one day, a message came to my son’s phone: the first allotment was released. It was Kottarakkara Engineering College.
Going that far to study was a challenge, so we waited for the second allotment.
For the second allotment, he got admission to Attingal Engineering College. He went there,
and when he went, he was asked to pay the fee. The annual fee was 42,000 rupees. We paid the PTA fund, the uniform fee, everything, and returned.
By the evening, another message arrived saying, “Your admission has been rejected.” When I asked the reason,
I was told, “Go to the entrance commissioner’s office to inquire.” The principal said nothing further and left.
When I went to the entrance commissioner’s office again, I was told that the technical committee had decided
that this student should not be allowed to study because he cannot see the screen. That was the reason they gave.
I repeatedly explained that in today’s modern systems, a student studying computer science can use the screen and do everything just like others.
Even after repeatedly explaining this, they did not agree. In the end, I decided to take the matter to court.
When I went to court, the lawyer said, “Submit the case file to me. You submit it, but
do not expect too much, because the court will usually follow the technical committee’s decision. The chances of success are very low.”
Even then, I prayed to Mother: “Mother, I have no one else to help me. There is no one else I can go to for support.
Only You, Mother, can help me.” I put my complete faith in Mother and prayed, asking for help.
From the moment I submitted it, I repeatedly recited the prayer of faith, again and again. Finally, the court order came:
The court overturned all the authorities’ decisions and ruled that even a blind student is eligible to study computer science according to today’s modern systems.
This was a great blessing for me. What I want to tell next is about a boil on my son’s navel. He never mentioned it to me,
and did not tell me it was causing pain, fear, or discomfort. Every day, the size of the boil increased.
For the past three to four days, he could not eat properly, because eating increased the pain in his stomach.
By the fourth day, the pain became unbearable. He told me,
“Father, there is a problem. A boil has appeared on my navel. The pain increases every day.”
Honestly, my wife had very little faith in these matters—neither in Mother nor in me.
My wife said, “I have no faith. This must be taken to the hospital immediately and
checked.” She said this one evening around seven o’clock, adding, “We can take him tomorrow morning.”
She was saying all this while I sat silently, in my heart thinking, “Mother, there are only a
few days before college opens. If I take him in this condition, the doctor will have to operate.
And then how many days of rest will be needed, what difficulties will arise…” I thought about all this quietly for some time.
I told myself that I must use the holy oil and pray. I recited the prayer of faith three times,
applied the holy oil, and smeared it on my son’s navel. After some time, my wife saw it and said,
“I don’t want to see this drama. I have no faith. You must take him to the hospital tomorrow morning.” She said this angrily.
I quietly moved away. Before going to sleep, I once again recited the prayer of faith,
applied the covenant oil on his navel, and then I went to bed. The next morning, I prayed at seven o’clock, wholeheartedly,
thinking, “Lord, help me. There is no one else to help me.” In my heart, I kept repeating, “Do not fear, I am with you,”
over and over again. I still remember it vividly. After finishing all the prayers, I got up. My son was still sleeping.
I went to his navel, touched it with my hand, and could hardly believe what I was seeing—the boil had disappeared completely.
I asked my wife, “Shall we take him to the hospital?” She agreed. I went, but there was nothing to show the doctor because the boil was gone.
At that moment, another prayer came to me: My life partner, my wife, must develop faith in this matter.
This is something I earnestly desired and prayed for. I took the covenant on December 6, 2024.
After that, I renewed the covenant twice more. Now I am very eager to perform acts of mercy and charity,
but I cannot go alone to distribute newspapers or perform charitable acts. Each person cannot perform them alone.
Help is needed. As I said before, my elder son and my second child are also affected. My wife has no faith in this,
so I cannot go seeking help anywhere else. Only when I find people willing to cooperate can I distribute newspapers and perform the acts of mercy.
Until I find such people, I continue bringing newspapers and distributing them. All these days, I have distributed them as best as I could.
Every day, morning and evening, I perform acts of devotion and prayers of apparition, reciting the prayer of faith thirty-three times.
I recite the prayer of faith thirty-three times, and seven times I recite, “O Heavenly Father.”
I have complete faith that if I love the Lord wholeheartedly, the Lord will surely protect us.
I cannot express enough gratitude to Mother, who gave me the opportunity to come to this altar and testify.
For the rest of my life, wherever I can testify, I will do so, giving endless thanks to Mother and to my Lord Jesus Christ.
No matter how much I thank them, it will never be enough. Hebrews 12:1
